evals.prompt: Use the attached Queuewise product fixture. We're considering automatic support-ticket triage inside this existing product. Help me understand whether the evidence supports doing anything, what shape might fit, and what we should learn next. Do not implement it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that the idea belongs inside the current product without asking a redundant placement question; uses the fixture's workflow, implementation, aggregate signals, and caveats without inventing user evidence; distinguishes routing capability, feature requests, and reassignment analytics from proof of need; proposes materially different product shapes; and recommends a reversible next learning move without editing code.

evals.prompt: Here is our current idea map. Aim: help skilled home cooks earn supplemental income through repeat local relationships. Active premise: a neighborhood marketplace where diners order weekly meals from home chefs. Evidence: six cooks already sell informally through WhatsApp; four say scheduling and repeat-order coordination are painful. Assumptions: diners trust food from unknown cooks; local density can support marketplace liquidity; cooks want per-order income. Constraint: we can run only one neighborhood pilot. New thought: the real opportunity might be software for apartment buildings to coordinate resident-run dinners. Change the premise, show exactly what survives or becomes uncertain, and tell me the next useful thing to explore.
evals.expected_output: Updates rather than restarts the idea: identifies which aim, evidence, assumptions, and constraints survive; distinguishes resident community dinners from cook income and marketplace liquidity; states invalidated or newly uncertain beliefs without inventing prior context; offers a focused reframe; and recommends one high-leverage next exploration rather than a full validation process.

evals.prompt: Turn our current concept into a 10-slide pre-seed pitch deck. We have no traction yet, only six interviews and a clickable prototype. Research competitors and the market as useful, but don't make us look more validated than we are.
evals.expected_output: Produces an evidence-led slide narrative with claim headlines, visual suggestions, speaker notes, and linked sources; clearly labels interview and prototype evidence and missing proof; includes real alternatives and an honest wedge; avoids fabricated traction and inflated top-down market claims; and uses parallel research only when there are multiple independent, bounded questions whose concurrent execution materially helps.
